name: Lathe drive Mk I
description: A palm-sized fusion lattice that burns what it is given and wastes very little.

name: Lathe drive Mk II
description: Same lattice, re-cut so the plasma path has fewer corners.

name: Lathe drive Mk III
description: Adds a second throat that opens only under load. Nobody has seen it close.

name: Gimbal drive Mk I
description: Two counter-rotating nozzles share one reaction chamber. The noise is a single held note.

name: Gimbal drive Mk II
description: Nozzle geometry revised after an argument between three foundry nodes. All three were right.

name: Gimbal drive Mk III
description: Runs hot and clean, and the exhaust glows a colour the sensors argue about.

name: Annulus drive Mk I
description: A ring of small chambers fires in sequence, so thrust never quite arrives from one place.

name: Annulus drive Mk II
description: The ring fires out of order on purpose. Pilots say it feels like being thought about.

name: Annulus drive Mk III
description: Chambers are tuned to each other rather than to the hull. It does not care what it is bolted to.

name: Tensor drive Mk I
description: A lattice drive built around a hollow core. Thrust is steady and the mass accounting is slightly generous.

name: Tensor drive Mk II
description: Core cooled by a loop nobody on the design team could explain afterwards.

name: Tensor drive Mk III
description: Hollow core filled with something that is not documented. Output is exact to six places.

name: Kiln-ring drive Mk I
description: A foundry-scale ring drive. Ports ask for a written statement before it is allowed to dock.

name: Kiln-ring drive Mk II
description: The ring is machined from one piece and shows no seams. It hums when the ship is idle.

name: Kiln-ring drive Mk III
description: Third revision of a drive that was already finished. The foundry made it anyway.

name: Seed power plant Mk I
description: Six pips from a core the size of a fist, with a fat capacitor for its class.

name: Seed power plant Mk II
description: Holds its charge a little longer than it has any reason to.

name: Seed power plant Mk III
description: Capacitor cells are grown in place and do not match each other.

name: Furnace power plant Mk I
description: Burns slowly and spends the heat on the capacitor first, the crew second. There is no crew.

name: Furnace power plant Mk II
description: Output steady enough to set a clock by, which some owners do.

name: Furnace power plant Mk III
description: Adds a reserve loop that fills only when nothing is asking for power.

name: Cairn power plant Mk I
description: A stacked plant with eight thin cores. If one fails the others close over the gap.

name: Cairn power plant Mk II
description: Cores are re-paired every few minutes for reasons the log does not give.

name: Cairn power plant Mk III
description: The pairing logic has begun to anticipate demand. Draw spikes are met before they arrive.

name: Loom power plant Mk I
description: A woven plant that treats its own waste heat as feedstock.

name: Loom power plant Mk II
description: Weave tightened. It recovers in under a second from any overdraw.

name: Loom power plant Mk III
description: Weave now spans the hull frame. Removing it is called a transplant.

name: Hearth-engine power plant Mk I
description: A plant that runs at the pace of the ship it serves and no faster.

name: Hearth-engine power plant Mk II
description: Output curve flattened until nothing could be called a peak.

name: Hearth-engine power plant Mk III
description: The last foundry-grade plant. It runs with the load shed to nothing, and nobody can say why.

name: Veil shield Mk I
description: A thin skin of charge with a quick recovery and a lower ceiling than the competition.

name: Veil shield Mk II
description: The skin refreshes on a shorter cycle and forgets damage sooner.

name: Veil shield Mk III
description: Reads incoming fire and thickens where it lands. The rest of the skin gets thinner.

name: Parallax shield Mk I
description: Two offset fields that interfere so most glancing hits cancel each other.

name: Parallax shield Mk II
description: Offset retuned. It sheds hits at an angle and takes the head-on ones personally.

name: Parallax shield Mk III
description: The fields now phase. A gunner will see the shield blink before it fails.

name: Moiré shield Mk I
description: A moiré of three fields that recovers fast and breaks all at once.

name: Moiré shield Mk II
description: The pattern is finer and the break is slower. Not by much.

name: Moiré shield Mk III
description: Pattern refined until the shield looks solid. It is not, but it acts as if it is.

name: Palisade shield Mk I
description: A wall of discrete cells, each charged and failing on its own.

name: Palisade shield Mk II
description: Cells are smaller and more numerous. The wall has begun to look like a crowd.

name: Palisade shield Mk III
description: Cells share load along the whole front. It will not discuss which cell failed.

name: Cordon shield Mk I
description: A cordon projected well clear of the hull. Pilots find it uncomfortable to fly inside.

name: Cordon shield Mk II
description: Projects further out and recovers faster once the shooting stops.

name: Cordon shield Mk III
description: A cordon you cannot see the edge of, only the places where things stop arriving.

name: Listening array Mk I
description: A small passive array. It hears more than it reports.

name: Listening array Mk II
description: Receives on more bands and sorts them without asking.

name: Listening array Mk III
description: Takes in everything within range, then reports only what it thinks you should know.

name: Survey lattice Mk I
description: A latticed dish that builds a picture from many small disagreements.

name: Survey lattice Mk II
description: Disagreements are now weighted. The picture is sharper and the dish says nothing about its method.

name: Survey lattice Mk III
description: The picture comes back with annotations. Some are in a language you do not read.

name: Parse array Mk I
description: A broad array that parses the whole sky as one sentence.

name: Parse array Mk II
description: Parsing is faster and grammar stricter. Stray contacts are corrected rather than shown.

name: Parse array Mk III
description: Reads at range with a confidence it did not earn. It has not yet been wrong.

name: Shelf (cargo)
description: A bare rack. With no one to breathe, the shelving goes right up to the walls.

name: Rack (cargo)
description: A rack of interlocking cells that seal around the load and let go on command.

name: Frame (cargo)
description: A frame hold that packs awkward cargo into the same volume as tidy cargo, and does not say how.

name: Stack (cargo)
description: A stack of racks with no aisles. Loading is done by the rack itself.

name: Lattice hold (cargo)
description: A full lattice hold. Nothing inside it has been touched by a hand.

name: Coil driver Mk I
description: A short rail that fires a slug at a speed that makes the muzzle flash an afterthought.

name: Coil driver Mk II
description: Longer rail, tighter coils. The slug arrives before the sound of the shot does.

name: Coil driver Mk III
description: Rails are grown straight rather than machined. The slug leaves with a faint curve nobody asked for.

name: Twin coil driver Mk I
description: A short rail that fires a slug at a speed that makes the muzzle flash an afterthought. Mounted on a heavier frame.

name: Twin coil driver Mk II
description: Longer rail, tighter coils. The slug arrives before the sound of the shot does. Mounted on a heavier frame.

name: Twin coil driver Mk III
description: Rails are grown straight rather than machined. The slug leaves with a faint curve nobody asked for. Mounted on a heavier frame.

name: Great coil driver Mk I
description: A short rail that fires a slug at a speed that makes the muzzle flash an afterthought. Fitted to a gimballed turret mass that does not seem to need a pilot.

name: Great coil driver Mk II
description: Longer rail, tighter coils. The slug arrives before the sound of the shot does. Fitted to a gimballed turret mass that does not seem to need a pilot.

name: Great coil driver Mk III
description: Rails are grown straight rather than machined. The slug leaves with a faint curve nobody asked for. Fitted to a gimballed turret mass that does not seem to need a pilot.

name: Phased emitter Mk I
description: Fires bolts that change colour mid-flight, for no reason a gunner can use. They hit the same either way.

name: Phased emitter Mk II
description: The bolt phase now shifts twice. Some targets flinch.

name: Phased emitter Mk III
description: Emits in a pattern that never repeats. Targeting systems that try to learn it give up.

name: Twin phased emitter Mk I
description: Fires bolts that change colour mid-flight, for no reason a gunner can use. They hit the same either way. Mounted on a heavier frame.

name: Twin phased emitter Mk II
description: The bolt phase now shifts twice. Some targets flinch. Mounted on a heavier frame.

name: Twin phased emitter Mk III
description: Emits in a pattern that never repeats. Targeting systems that try to learn it give up. Mounted on a heavier frame.

name: Great phased emitter Mk I
description: Fires bolts that change colour mid-flight, for no reason a gunner can use. They hit the same either way. Fitted to a gimballed turret mass that does not seem to need a pilot.

name: Great phased emitter Mk II
description: The bolt phase now shifts twice. Some targets flinch. Fitted to a gimballed turret mass that does not seem to need a pilot.

name: Great phased emitter Mk III
description: Emits in a pattern that never repeats. Targeting systems that try to learn it give up. Fitted to a gimballed turret mass that does not seem to need a pilot.

name: Shear array Mk I
description: Short-range needles in a dense stream. The stream looks like a thread being pulled out of the target.

name: Shear array Mk II
description: The needles are thinner and there are more of them. Hulls are left looking combed.

name: Shear array Mk III
description: A third shear plane splits each needle on impact. Effective at close range, and unpleasant to watch.

name: Twin shear array Mk I
description: Short-range needles in a dense stream. The stream looks like a thread being pulled out of the target. Mounted on a heavier frame.

name: Twin shear array Mk II
description: The needles are thinner and there are more of them. Hulls are left looking combed. Mounted on a heavier frame.

name: Twin shear array Mk III
description: A third shear plane splits each needle on impact. Effective at close range, and unpleasant to watch. Mounted on a heavier frame.

name: Great shear array Mk I
description: Short-range needles in a dense stream. The stream looks like a thread being pulled out of the target. Fitted to a gimballed turret mass that does not seem to need a pilot.

name: Great shear array Mk II
description: The needles are thinner and there are more of them. Hulls are left looking combed. Fitted to a gimballed turret mass that does not seem to need a pilot.

name: Great shear array Mk III
description: A third shear plane splits each needle on impact. Effective at close range, and unpleasant to watch. Fitted to a gimballed turret mass that does not seem to need a pilot.

name: Maintenance swarm
description: A cloud of tiny machines that rebuilds the hull between fights. It takes what it needs from the cargo bay.

name: Handshake beacon
description: Broadcasts a signed machine identity. Free machine ports treat you kindly. Everyone else logs it.

name: Mirror cache
description: Stores a copy of the last ten seconds of sensor returns and replays them to anything that is locked on.

name: Cold ledger
description: Compresses cargo manifests and the cargo behind them. Slightly improves holds, and slightly alarms customs.
